mathematical_result: The actual canonical coordinate heat-bath output law equals normalized target restriction on every positive retained-coordinate fiber.
theorem_delta: heatBath X mu i x = cond mu {y | retained_i y = retained_i x}; finite dependent coordinate count, finite mu, selected-only Nonempty/StandardBorel, retained-product measurable singletons, and explicit nonzero fiber mass.
exact_elaborated_proposition: ∀ {n : ℕ} (X : Fin (n + 1) → Type u_1) [inst : (j : Fin (n + 1)) → MeasurableSpace (X j)] (μ : Measure ((j : Fin (n + 1)) → X j)) [inst_1 : IsFiniteMeasure μ] (i : Fin (n + 1)) [inst_2 : StandardBorelSpace (X i)] [inst_3 : Nonempty (X i)] [MeasurableSingletonClass ((j : Fin n) → X (i.succAbove j))] (x : (j : Fin (n + 1)) → X j), μ {y | (fun j => y (i.succAbove j)) = fun j => x (i.succAbove j)} ≠ 0 → (CoordinateHeatBath.heatBath X μ i) x = μ[|{y | (fun j => y (i.succAbove j)) = fun j => x (i.succAbove j)}]
minimal_anonymous_definition_context: Fin (n+1) is the index type; i.succAbove : Fin n → Fin(n+1) enumerates all indices other than i in increasing order.
e_i is the measurable equivalence x ↦ ((fun j => x(i.succAbove j)), x i), with inverse reinserting the selected coordinate.

For ν = μ.map e_i, κ = condDistrib Prod.snd Prod.fst ν; condDistrib Y X ν is the selected regular conditional-distribution Markov kernel, defined as the conditional kernel of ν.map(fun a => (X a,Y a)).
CoordinateHeatBath.heatBath X μ i x = (e_i.symm)_#(dirac((e_i x).1) × κ((e_i x).1)); measure map means pushforward.
μ[|s] means ProbabilityTheory.cond μ s, defined by (μ s)⁻¹ • μ.restrict s; scalars are ENNReal with totalized inverse.

Evaluate the pushforward rectangle and cond_apply' to expose the same denominator.
Identify the rectangle preimage with retained fiber intersect output event, by e.symm_apply_apply.
